subject: Genetics
title: Polygenic Risk Scores
description: A quick win: understand Polygenic Risk Scores.

hook.text: No single gene causes heart disease. But combine thousands of tiny genetic effects, and a risk score emerges.

buildup.text: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) sum up the influence of millions of DNA variants into one number predicting disease risk.

discovery.text: A high PRS for heart disease identifies people at 3x the average risk—even if they have no family history.

twist.text: PRS are built mostly from European data. They predict poorly for African and Asian populations. Bias is baked in.

climax.text: Critics say PRS give false precision. A 30% risk feels exact but isn't.

punchline.text: Million variants. One score. Uncertain meaning.

quiz.question: What is a major limitation of current polygenic risk scores?
